name: Hypatia
note: Philosopher and astronomer in Alexandria. Taught and preserved Greek geometry and edited works on conics.

name: Aryabhata
note: Indian astronomer-mathematician. Gave a refined value of pi and built early sine tables.

name: Liu Hui
note: Commentator on the Nine Chapters on the Mathematical Art. Devised a polygon method for pi.

name: Brahmagupta
note: Formalized rules for zero and negative numbers; gave general solutions to quadratics.

name: Virahanka
note: Studied Sanskrit poetic metre; described the recurrence later known as the Fibonacci sequence.

name: Al-Khwarizmi
note: Father of algebra. Gave systematic methods for solving linear and quadratic equations.

name: Al-Biruni
note: Polymath who measured Earth's radius and advanced trigonometry and geodesy.

name: Omar Khayyam
note: Solved cubic equations geometrically by intersecting conic sections; reformed the Persian calendar.

name: Bhaskara II
note: Wrote the Lilavati and Bijaganita; the chakravala method solved a hard class of equations.

name: Al-Karaji
note: Freed algebra from geometric proof; worked on the binomial theorem and arithmetic series.

name: Abu'l-Wafa al-Buzjani
note: Advanced trigonometry and spherical geometry; compiled tangent-function tables.
formula: sin t, cos t, tan t

name: Gangesa Upadhyaya
note: Founder of the Navya-Nyaya school; built a rigorous formal theory of inference.

name: Narayana Pandita
note: Wrote on magic squares, combinatorics, and algebraic identities.

name: Madhava of Sangamagrama
note: Founded the Kerala school; found infinite series for pi and trig functions, anticipating calculus.

name: Jamshid al-Kashi
note: Computed pi to sixteen decimal places and advanced decimal fractions and astronomical tables.

name: Seki Takakazu
note: Founder of wasan, Japan's native mathematical tradition; pioneered work on determinants.

name: Sophie Germain
note: Worked under a male pseudonym; advanced elasticity theory and a special case of Fermat's Last Theorem.

name: Alexander Grothendieck
note: Rebuilt algebraic geometry from its foundations with schemes, sheaves, and topos theory.

name: Shinichi Mochizuki
note: Number theorist working in arithmetic geometry; proposed inter-universal Teichmuller theory toward the ABC conjecture.
